# Nexus v1.96.5 Experimental leaderboard sync

This release changes how stored DPS history moves between Nexus users. It is an experimental prerelease.

## Quick changelog

- Added experimental direct sync for current clients, with ACK, timeout, and
  automatic `wrbuildssync` fallback. It remains off by default.
- Fixed leaderboard best-record rejection, owner-versus-relay evidence,
  generation handling, and old/new digest reconciliation.
- Improved level-80 Echo sensing. Orb changes now refresh Progress, Still
  Needed, and To Shed without resaving the build. A qualifying higher-quality
  Echo satisfies a lower stored target; lower-quality Echoes cannot satisfy a
  higher target.
- Added quality-colored full tooltips, unclipped HUD text, and build-preview
  Echo tooltips.
- Preserved imported locked-Echo intent through the editor and save path.
- Added visible, persistent controls for direct sync and automatic Saved Build
  updates. Both default off, and both report changes in chat.

## Defaults and controls

- Experimental direct sync uses ordinary chat whispers and defaults off.
  To try it, open Nexus, click the three dots (`...`) in the top-left, and set
  `Direct sync (experimental)` to ON on both current clients. In manual mode,
  run `/nexus sync` on both characters so both sync sessions are open. The
  slash-command equivalent is `/nexus syncdirect on`. Turning it off returns
  bulk responses to `wrbuildssync`.
- Automatic Saved Build updates default off for new or missing settings.
  Existing saved preferences are preserved. Check the HUD settings menu's
  `Automatic Saved Build updates: ON/OFF` before testing with valuable builds.
- Automatic locking remains a separate option that defaults off.
- Sync retains its conservative pace and resting/combat restrictions.
- The development `/nexuslab` tool is excluded from the player package.

## Read before installing

Back up `NexusDB` and `WishlistRealizerDB` before testing. If Nexus causes stutter, long syncs, FPS loss, or unusual memory use, report it to me with your Sync diagnostics and `/nexus perf` output, then reinstall v1.96.4. Existing SavedVariables remain compatible with the rollback.

## How sync works now

- Your own addon still records only your highest DPS for each encounter. Weaker attempts do not replace your saved best.
- Each new owner record receives a server timestamp. During replication, the newest owner snapshot wins.
- Current clients can relay stored DPS records while the original player is offline. Repeated relays preserve the owner's timestamp.
- Records sent directly by v1.19.5 players remain compatible. Older clients cannot carry third-party history and may continue showing their older highest score until they update.
- Relayed history remains marked unverified until the character sends the record directly.
- Enhanced peers exchange full exact relay evidence over either channel or
  negotiated whisper transport. Historical catalog removal does not by itself
  prevent a valid record from transferring; records without valid evidence can
  still be rejected.
- Failed or unacknowledged direct transfers replay canonical WLRB/WLD2 on the
  channel. Duplicate delivery cannot downgrade equivalent owner evidence.
- Bucket hashes, responder claims, paced queues, and two quiet unchanged passes keep sync work bounded.

The runtime addon, installed folder, slash commands, and SavedVariables remain
`Nexus`. This release does not reset SavedVariables. Automatic Saved Build
updates can overwrite only the active server-confirmed slot when explicitly
enabled, so the option now defaults off and is visible in the settings menu.

## Display fixes

- At level 80, Nexus follows the most recently changed live Echo source. Orb
  results refresh Progress, Still Needed, and To Shed within the normal local
  polling window, without resaving or reopening the HUD. A later Saved Build
  activation takes precedence again.
- Qualifying higher-quality variants count toward lower stored wishlist targets
  and stay out of To Shed. Lower-quality variants cannot satisfy higher targets.
- Echo previews expose spell, quality, stack, and locked-state tooltips.
- Needed/Shed lists display quality colors and full hover text. Clipped status
  and recommendation lines expose their complete text on hover.

Same-faction whisper delivery has succeeded in live testing, but failure,
mixed-client, and full-history convergence checks remain experimental. Offline
tests do not establish private-server throttle behavior or complete live safety.
